trial_court: Additional District Judge-01, West Delhi, HMA No.204/2012
case_name: Devinder Singh Narula vs Meenakshi Nangia
facts_of_case: The parties filed a joint petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, seeking dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: This Court can invoke its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution in an irreconcilable situation to do complete justice between the parties.
legal_principles.held: In fact, in the case of Kiran vs. Sharad Dutt [(2000) 10 SCC 243], which was considered in Anil Kumar Jain's case, after living separately for many years and 11 years after initiating proceedings under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, the parties filed a joint application before this Court for leave to amend the divorce petition and to convert the same into a proceeding under Section 13-B of the Act.

legal_principles.principle: Technicality should be tempered by pragmatism if substantive justice is to be done to the parties.
legal_principles.held: It was urged that technicality should be tampered by pragmatism, if substantive justice was to be done to the parties.
cited_cases: Anil Kumar Jain vs. Maya Jain, [(2009) 10 SCC 415]

outcome.final_order: The Supreme Court granted a decree of divorce declaring the marriage to be dissolved with effect from the date of the decree.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act provisions
